searchText: <@!372731338031366165> about eth2stats, what's out there to set up: - dashboard. I forked it so it builds on github pages (with github action), so it doesn't require the old nginx setup, and you can reference external dashboards in header + be clear about git fork info. You can fork https://github.com/protolambda/pyrmont.eth2.wtf for the latest styling/fixes, and a working config as example. I still need to merge those changes back into my open PR here: https://github.com/ConsenSys/eth2stats-dashboard/pull/1 There is a config file to define server endpoint, linked dashboards and fork info. And there is a CNAME file to configure the domain. You can also run it locally (use npm commands for hot-reloads etc.), and point it to a local server instead by using an environment var. - client: works as-is, hosted on https://github.com/Alethio/eth2stats-client (you can use upstream docker image) - server: collects clients metrics, and exposes a grpc (for client input) and http (for dashboard serving) endpoint. The websocket is available via upgrade on that same http ednpoint, but was always was a WIP, and doesn't actually do anything but connecting (not my idea). My fork has a branch with some experimental fixes and geo-ip update. If I voluntary exit, I know I cannot withdraw my ETH back to ETH1. However, can I re-enter as a validator? For example, if I know I won't be able to run my validator for a couple months (for reasons), can I voluntarily exit and then voluntarily enter a couple months later? No, voluntary exits are currently irreversible You'd have to either take the hit for being offline, or find another way to keep validating Is there a mechanism design reason for this, or just engineering cost/complexity that we wanted to avoid in phase 0? Mostly the latter, having the ability for exited validators to be active again would add more complexity around the handling of validator indexes. It's derived from the mnemonic How can I have my withdraw address be a contract wallet rather than based on that mnemonic? e.g., set withdraw address to a Gnosis wallet or multisig or something. excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content:
<@!372731338031366165> about eth2stats, what's out there to set up:
- dashboard. I forked it so it builds on github pages (with github action), so it doesn't require the old nginx setup, and you can reference external dashboards in header + be clear about git fork info. You can fork https://github.com/protolambda/pyrmont.eth2.wtf for the latest styling/fixes, and a working config as example. I still need to merge those changes back into my open PR here: https://github.com/ConsenSys/eth2stats-dashboard/pull/1 There is a config file to define server endpoint, linked dashboards and fork info. And there is a CNAME file to configure the domain. You can also run it locally (use npm commands for hot-reloads etc.), and point it to a local server instead by using an environment var.
- client: works as-is, hosted on https://github.com/Alethio/eth2stats-client (you can use upstream docker image)
- server: collects clients metrics, and exposes a grpc (for client input) and http (for dashboard serving) endpoint. The websocket is available via upgrade on that same http ednpoint, but was always was a WIP, and doesn't actually do anything but connecting (not my idea). My fork has a branch with some experimental fixes and geo-ip update.
